ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, two lines are intersected by three parallel lines, with $DE = 4$, $EF = 6$, and $AB = 2$. What is the value of $AC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given: $l_1 \parallel l_2$,\\
Therefore, $\frac{DE}{EF}=\frac{AB}{BC}$,\\
Therefore, $\frac{4}{6}=\frac{2}{BC}$,\\
Therefore, $BC=3$,\\
Therefore, $AC=AB+BC=2+3=\boxed{5}$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as three parallel lines l1, l2, l3 cut by two slanted transversals. On the rising transversal, the consecutive intersections are A on l1, B on l2, C on l3; on the falling transversal, the corresponding consecutive intersections are D on l1, E on l2, F on l3. Use the intercept theorem for parallel lines: corresponding segments cut off on any two transversals are proportional, so DE/EF = AB/BC. Substitute the text-given lengths DE = 4, EF = 6, AB = 2 to get 4/6 = 2/BC, hence BC = 3. Then AC is the whole segment from A to C on the same transversal, so AC = AB + BC = 2 + 3 = 5.
